title: Interrogatory Publication Admission
subject: Evidence
stem: On February 3, Lydia, the owner of a catering company, sued Peter, a former wholesale supplier, in state court over disputed rebate charges. Peter served written interrogatories under the state code of civil procedure. Interrogatory 7 asked Lydia to list her company's gross receipts for each month during the four-year period in dispute. Lydia answered, "The monthly gross receipts are set out in the Metro Banquet Market Report." Before trial, the court took judicial notice that the report was a reputable source whose catering-sales listings were treated as reliable by informed people in the industry. At trial, Peter offers the report pages listing Lydia's monthly receipts. Lydia objects.
call: The court should rule that the report pages are

choices.A: inadmissible, because the report's monthly figures have not been independently proved accurate.
choices.B: admissible as an admission by a party.
choices.C: admissible, because the report was established as a reputable source normally relied on by informed people.
choices.D: inadmissible as hearsay not covered by any exception.

rightExplanation: Lydia's answer made the market-report pages admissible against her. A party's own statement, when offered by an opposing party, is an admission and is excluded from hearsay under FRE 801(d)(2). Her interrogatory response did more than point Peter toward a possible source; it adopted the report's monthly receipts as the answer to the question. Peter therefore may offer the relevant pages as Lydia's admission. The separate judicial-notice ruling helps explain why the report seemed reliable, but the admissibility ground that resolves the objection is Lydia's adoption of the figures in discovery.

wrongExplanations.A: The independent-accuracy objection fits the publication facts, but Lydia supplied the publication as her own discovery answer. Party admissions do not require separate proof that the statement is accurate before admission.
wrongExplanations.C: The judicial-notice ruling is the strongest lure because the court found the report reputable. The offered pages are admissible because Lydia adopted them, not merely because the publication is well regarded.
wrongExplanations.D: The hearsay label has force because Peter offers out-of-court sales figures for their truth. An opposing party's adopted statement is excluded from hearsay under FRE 801(d)(2).
